newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet sell off a "political game" - Amato.
newsitem.headline: Stet sell off a "political game" - Amato.

text.p: The privatisation of telecoms holding Stet, planned for 1997, has become a political football, the head of Italy's antitrust authority said on Wednesday.
"Naturally political games are involved here," Giuliano Amato said in an interview with state radio.
The government hopes to sell off Stet by the end of next March, but before the flotation can go ahead parliament must approve a bill setting up a watchdog authority for the sector.
The draft law has had a rough ride through parliament, changing shape on a number of occasions. It is now tied to a contested bill covering new television ownership rules.
Stet Managing Director Ernesto Pascale warned earlier this month that unless the authority was approved by the end of November, there would not be enough time to meet the flotation timetable.
"If someone doesn't want the privatisation of Stet, and knows that before the privatisation the authority has to be set up, they can try to delay the launch of the authority," Amato told the radio.
However, he said electricity utility Enel could be sold off next year, as planned.
"Theoretically, the privatisation of Enel is possible because the authority is in place...the trouble is that there needs to be a solid accord on the whole affair," Amato said.
Enel's recently appointed chairman Chicco Testa said at the weekend that his group's privatisation should be linked to the sector's liberalisation.

He said that without adequate competitiveness, privatisation would merely convert the state monopoly over the sector into a private monopoly and called for the electricity system to be reorganised, with Enel broken up into different divisions.
The government is seeking to sell Enel in one piece and analysts warn that any break-up would delay the sale by up to two years, or even more. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
